candidates.reason: Single firsthand source (dicasdouruguai.com.br) names the 08:30 Buenos Aires-Colonia departure as the most crowded and recommends a mid-morning sailing instead; useful but not independently corroborated within budget, so kept shortlisted rather than shipped as a firm tip.

candidates.name: José Ignacio
candidates.reason: Quieter, more upscale beach town roughly 30-40 minutes from central Punta del Este; positioned as a day-trip pairing with the traveler's stated interest in the Punta del Este beach scene, not a replacement for it.

candidates.name: La Pedrera
candidates.reason: Mentioned as a cheaper, calmer beach-town alternative further from the trip's three named cities. Only one source found (Ohlalá!, Feb 2025) and not independently corroborated — flagged as a lead, not shipped.

candidates.name: Laguna Garzón
candidates.reason: Protected-area lagoon with kayak/SUP/birdwatching tours run by certified local guides, past José Ignacio on the coastal road toward Rocha; fits the nature/outdoors priority as a day trip from Punta del Este.

candidates.name: Isla de Lobos
candidates.reason: Mainstream sea-lion boat excursion already covered by national press (Infobae and Canal26, both Jan 2025); fails the anti-default filter for Pass B — likely already a Pass A pick, not a novel Pass B find.

candidates.name: Cabo Polonio
candidates.reason: Genuinely novel, off-grid nature find (no electricity or direct road access, large sea lion colony) but sits roughly 150km east of Punta del Este, requiring an overnight detour outside this trip's 8-night Montevideo/Colonia/Punta del Este shape — a lead worth remembering for a future, longer trip, not this one.

evidence.claim: Buenos Aires day-tripper ferries land and depart Colonia between roughly 10:00 and 15:00; arriving before 10:00 or staying past 16:00 shows a visibly quieter, more photogenic old town once the day-trip crowd has left.

Colonia's historic quarter gets 'MUITO mais mágica' (much more magical) in the late afternoon and evening, once the same-day ferry tourists ('bate-volta') have already left; the author frames overnighting there as the way to see the town at its best.
The 08:30 Buenos Aires-Colonia ferry departure is the most crowded of the day; the author recommends a mid-morning sailing instead. Single-sourced within this pass, not independently corroborated.
Mercado Agrícola de Montevideo (MAM) is open daily 09:00-22:00 overall, with the gastronomy section 11:00-23:00 and shops 10:00-22:00, at José L. Terra 2220.

MAM is 'mais moderno, mistura gastronomia com mercado de verdade. Frequentado por moradores locais' — attracts local residents, in contrast to Mercado del Puerto, which the same author calls 'mais antigo, mais turístico.' Weekdays Tue-Fri are quieter than Saturdays.

MAM is 'another good option in the city and is less touristic' than Mercado del Puerto, and 'a more complete market' with broader food/shop offerings. Published Sept 2021 — outside the 24-month experiential-freshness window, recorded as a re-verify lead rather than current corroboration.
Lo de Silverio (Alejo Rossell y Rius 1655 esquina 4 de Julio, Villa Dolores) is open Tuesday-Saturday 12:00-16:00 and 20:00-00:00, Sunday 12:00-16:00.

José Ignacio stays 'discreto, lindo y curado' in February — busy but noticeably less intense than January's peak; recommended for long lunches and a quieter register than central Punta, best visited as a day trip while staying in Punta (Mansa or the Península) for practicality.

'Las playas de José Ignacio son menos concurridas, ofreciendo un entorno más sereno' compared to Punta del Este's nightlife-driven, crowd-seeking scene — José Ignacio draws travelers wanting privacy and calm rather than the multitudes.
La Pedrera has 'more middle-class presence,' is 'más gasoleras' (less flashy) than Punta del Este, and its lack of large nightclubs keeps a calmer, safer atmosphere. Single-sourced within this pass.

Laguna Garzón's local operator runs kayak, SUP, and canoe outings on the lagoon plus guided birdwatching, forest-bathing walks, and astronomy sessions; booking is by WhatsApp/contact form with 'cupos limitados' (limited capacity) and no fixed public schedule beyond checking the next available date.

Uruguayan Spanish uses voseo ('vos' + 'tenés'/'sos' conjugations, not 'tú'). Everyday words a first-time visitor will hear: botija/gurí (kid), championes (sneakers), bondi (bus), buzo (sweater), tá (filler, short for 'está'), al mango (full-on/maxed out), de más (excellent — positive, unlike standard Spanish usage).

reservations.walkIn: Not walk-in — the operator requires advance booking via WhatsApp/contact form due to limited capacity per outing and does not publish a fixed daily schedule ('consultá la próxima fecha').
reservations.alternatives: Turismo Rocha (turismorocha.gub.uy) lists the same protected-area activities under the government tourism portal for the department, as an alternative discovery/contact route if the operator's own channel is unresponsive — not independently fetched this pass.

reservations.walkIn: Not explicitly confirmed on the official site; phone (+598 2628 4771) and email are listed for contact but no stated walk-in policy — calling ahead is advisable for dinner-service hours (20:00-00:00) given ~100-guest capacity and live-music nights.

transport.notApplicableReason: This pass covers Montevideo-Colonia-Punta del Este domestic connections (bus and the Buenos Aires-Colonia ferry as a crowd-timing factor, not a booked leg for this itinerary); all are routine and forgiving, so no route rose to R3+ risk requiring transport-depth research in this pass.

saturation.note: Final search round (Isla de Lobos boat tours, traditional Sunday-asado timing) returned mainstream press coverage already surfaced or generic cultural background with no new resident-angle specifics — a duplicates/weaker signal. Several native-language aggregator leads (Don Beto, La Otra Parrilla, Pellicer, Asados Iruña, La Pedrera) remain single- or zero-sourced and were recorded as rejected/considered/shortlisted rather than pushed further, since none is load-bearing enough to change the shipped/detour picks (Mercado Agrícola de Montevideo as shortlisted, Lo de Silverio, Colonia's off-peak visit window, José Ignacio, Laguna Garzón). Stopping here; unresolved single-source leads are recorded honestly, not silently dropped or promoted.

nativeLanguage.why: Uruguay's resident/blog layer writes in Spanish, plus a large body of firsthand Brazilian Portuguese travel blogging aimed at the huge Argentine/Brazilian day-tripper audience that dominates Colonia and Punta del Este. English top-10 sources are Pass A's territory and under-sample local crowd-timing tactics and off-default food/nature picks.
